title: DS-Lite Security: a Reproducible Full-Stack Attack Testbed, 12 Executed Attacks, a Three-Attribute Classification, and Verified Mitigations
description: Reproducible artifact for the article "A Verified, Reproducible Security Analysis of Dual-Stack Lite Across the Data, Control, and Management Planes" (submitted to Computers & Security). Contains the Docker testbed realizing the DS-Lite (RFC 6333) reference architecture across the data, control, and management planes; 12 attack tools spanning softwire spoofing/interception/injection/relay, fragment-reassembly poisoning, PCP third-party abuse and cross-subscriber enumeration, DNS and DHCPv6 AFTR-discovery hijacking, and DS-Lite MIB access over SNMP; an independent verifier (packet captures plus direct reads of the AFTR and B4 state, and observed device behavior) with the per-attack reference captures for the baseline, every attack, and every mitigation before and after it is applied; the three-attribute attack classification (Attack Surface, Provenance, Blast Radius), with Attacker Position read as a deployment vantage, and its classifier and quality-verification scripts; one attack-defense tree per attack rendered with QuADTool; and the verified, reversible mitigations with their apply/verify scripts, including DECAP-BIND, the decapsulation-time source binding that instantiates the softwire ingress filter RFC 6333 leaves optional. Three further generic-CGNAT weaknesses (shared-address reputation poisoning, PCP port exhaustion, PCP epoch spoofing) are retained as supplementary tools, documented but outside the paper's executed corpus. The article is self-contained; this archive holds the supporting detail and regenerates every numerical result and capture.
